extracted.intended_audience: researchers and students planning to preregister studies (OSF users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting preregistration records and templates on the Open Science Framework (OSF), including general preregistration, systematic review registrations, and non-interventional evidence synthesis protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify your research plan in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: "When you preregister your research, you're simply specifying your research plan in advance of your study and submitting it to a registry."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preregistration requires documenting the study plan (hypotheses, methods, analysis) before data collection/analysis to reduce undisclosed flexibility; the page points users to templates and registries (OSF) where plans are submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate exploratory (hypothesis-generating) from confirmatory (hypothesis-testing) research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both exploratory and confirmatory research are important, but they should be distinguished because the same data should not be used to both generate and test a hypothesis. Failure to separate them can unintentionally reduce credibility; preregistration clarifies this distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use the same data to generate and test a hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: "The same data cannot be used to generate and test a hypothesis, which can happen unintentionally and reduce the credibility of your results."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specifying hypotheses and analysis plans prevents circular use of data. The page frames this as a core reason for preregistration: planning improves quality and transparency and supports clear reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit preregistration to a registry (e.g., OSF)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preregistrations should be recorded in an accessible registry. The guide highlights OSF as the platform and links to specific OSF templates/registration types for completing that submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the OSF Prereg* Template for general registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: "OSF Prereg* Template — This is a general registration template that can be used for any purpose."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For general-purpose preregistrations across study types, use the OSF Prereg* template available within OSF. The page lists this template as the default general registration option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Generalized Systematic Review Registration for systematic reviews and meta-analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: "For preregistering systematic reviews and meta-analyses of research — For New Registrations you can select Generalized Systematic Review Registration and use the template within OSF."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preregistering systematic reviews or meta-analyses, choose the specialized Generalized Systematic Review Registration template in OSF to capture review-specific protocol details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow NIROES guidelines for non-interventional, reproducible, open evidence synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: "Non-Interventional, Reproducible, and Open Evidence Synthesis (NIROES) — Guidelines for creating and pre-registering your protocol as well as writing your systematic review for non-interventional research."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-interventional evidence syntheses, use the NIROES guidance for both preregistration of protocols and for writing the systematic review. The page links to NIRO SR Guidelines as an authoritative resource.
